issue: Spurious 'no' label on the Request → Capability filter entry edge. The top row shows three horizontal arrows each labeled 'no', but the first arrow (Request → Capability filter) is an unconditional entry edge — a request always enters the capability filter. The two 'no' outcomes belong on Capability filter → Cost/SLO gate and Cost/SLO gate → Fallthrough only. As drawn, a reader can infer the request reaches the capability filter only when something earlier answers 'no', which inverts the cascade's entry condition.
evidence: Rendered page 315: the glyph 'no' sits above the arrow between the 'Request' box and the 'Capability filter' box (leftmost of the three 'no' labels), in addition to the two 'no' labels over the filter→gate and gate→fallthrough arrows. The caption and the prose below ('A request first passes a capability filter … then a cost/SLO gate … and otherwise falls through') describe an unconditional first stage with two conditional continuations — i.e., exactly two 'no' edges.
acceptance_test: In the rebuilt figure, the Request → Capability filter arrow carries no condition label; exactly two 'no' labels appear, one on Capability filter → Cost/SLO gate and one on Cost/SLO gate → Fallthrough; the 'yes → specialist' and 'yes → frontier / small' labels remain on their downward edges.

issue: Caption names three leaf families — 'the specialist, general and fallback model families as leaves' — but the diagram's leaves are labeled Embedding/Vision/Math/reason (specialist), Frontier/Small gen, and General. There is no leaf labeled or identifiable as a distinct 'fallback' family, and the middle group ('frontier / small') is not called 'general' anywhere in the figure. The caption's three-family taxonomy does not map onto the figure's three leaf groups.
evidence: Caption text: 'with the specialist, general and fallback model families as leaves'. Diagram leaf boxes: 'Embedding', 'Vision', 'Math/reason', 'Frontier', 'Small gen', 'General'. The prose below the figure says the request 'falls through to a general model', making 'General' the fallback leaf and leaving 'general' family = frontier/small unnamed in the figure — the two naming systems cross.
acceptance_test: Either the caption names the actual leaf groups ('specialist, frontier/small, and general-fallback leaves') or the figure labels its three groups with the caption's family names; in both caption and figure the same three terms identify the same three groups.

issue: Caption states the append-only context assumption 'from the 9,200-token prompt at 2.62 MB/token KV' without the precision qualifier. Per the book's canonical KV convention, 2.62 MB/token is the FP16 value (8-bit KV is ~1.31 MB/token). Figures 19.2 and 19.3 both label the same 2.62 figure explicitly as FP16; this caption does not, so a reader could read 2.62 as the book's default/canonical per-token KV.
evidence: Caption on PDF 318: 'an append-only context from the 9,200-token prompt at 2.62 MB/token KV'. Compare Fig 19.2 panel (b) axis 'KV / request (GB, FP16)', legend 'KV / request (FP16)', and Fig 19.3 axis 'FP16 KV / request after four agent turns (GB)', all of which qualify 2.62 as FP16.
acceptance_test: Caption reads 'at 2.62 MB/token FP16 KV' (or 'FP16 KV of 2.62 MB/token'), matching the precision labeling used in Figs 19.2 and 19.3.

issue: Inconsistent visual encoding of 'region': the unused-capacity area above S is solid-shaded pink and labeled 'UNUSED capacity', but the area beneath the served-demand curve that the blue label 'actually-served demand region' names appears unshaded (gridlines visible through it). One of the two named regions is filled, the other is only text floating over the plot background, so the label reads as pointing at an arbitrary spot rather than an area.
evidence: Rendered page 347: pink fill spans the area between S = 40 and C_analytic for N ≳ 22 with an explicit callout; the blue text 'actually-served demand region' sits at approximately N = 35–55, y ≈ 25 with no corresponding fill or leader line visible under the S curve.
acceptance_test: Either the area under the S curve receives a light fill (or hatch) matching the label 'region' and distinguishable from the unused-capacity fill in grayscale, or the label is reworded/repositioned (e.g., arrow to the S curve) so it does not claim a shaded region that is not drawn.
